name: Sika Masonry AU 1
paste:
SIKA® MASONRY AU 1: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sika® Masonry AU 1, April 2023, Version 01.02 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/q/sika_masonry_au_1.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sika® Masonry AU 1 where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02).
1.2 Product description. Sika® Masonry AU 1 is a High Performance water repelling and efflorescence reducing admixture for various masonry / concrete applications.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sika® Masonry AU 1 is a High Efficiency Masonry / Concrete admixture that can be used for efflorescence reduction, absorption control and water repellency.
1.4 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - Typical applications are.
    - Dry and Semi-dry cast applications:
    - Concrete masonry units
    - Pavers
1.5 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - Wet cast applications.
    - Stone veneer
    - Architectural precast
1.6 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - Aesthetics.
    - Use of Sika® Masonry AU 1 may improve colour brightness

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sika® Masonry AU 1
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Water Repelling and Efflorescence Reducing Admixture
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (April 2023, Version 01.02) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer. Sika® Masonry AU 1 is suitable for the production of dry or wet cast Masonry / Concrete. Use of Sika® Masonry AU-1 results in:
    - Improved water repellency
    - Reduced efflorescence
    - Increased durability
    - Improved aesthetics (brighter colours)
    - Improved / Reduced production rates / Cycle times
2.4 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Appearance and colour: White liquid
    - Specific gravity: 0.97 g/cm³approximately
2.5 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 1000 litre IBC; 205 litre drum; 10 litre container
    - Shelf life: Shelf life, when stored in dry warehouse conditions between 5°C and 35°C, is six (6) months.
2.6 Storage conditions. Sika® Masonry AU 1 should be stored at temperature above 5°C and regularly recirculated , twice a day or as per our Technical Service instructions. If frozen, admixture cannot be re-constituted and must be discarded according to local laws.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 Substrate preparation. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (April 2023, Version 01.02) states no substrate preparation requirements.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02) and the requirements below.
4.2 Recommended dosage. Dosage rate will vary according to targeted application. Normally a dosage range of 200 - 500 ml / 100 kg of cementitious material should be sufficient for efflorescence and absorption control. If water repellency is required dosage may be increased to 750 ml - 2000 ml /100 kg of cementitious material . Actual dosage rate will vary based upon mix design. Proper dosage should always be verified by trial batch to ensure desired performance is achieved. Dosages outside the recommended range may be used for special requirements and applications.
4.3 Dispensing. Sika® Masonry AU 1 should be added with the batching water or introduced at the end of the mixing process. For concrete containing a low water content and applications that have a very low water cement ratio, it is necessary to provide sufficient mixing time to allow the admixture to be distributed throughout the entire batch and provide uniform performance. In general, a total mixing time of at least 90 seconds is essential. Mixing time after adding the admixture depends on the individual circumstances and should be determined by trials. Do not introduce Sika® Masonry AU 1 up front, or directly onto dry cementitious materials, as this may reduce admixture performance.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, confirm the site conditions with the manufacturer. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Conditions to be verified. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (April 2023, Version 01.02) lists no application condition limits.
5.3 Trials, test areas and compatibility checks stated by the manufacturer.
    - Dosage rate will vary according to targeted application. Normally a dosage range of 200 - 500 ml / 100 kg of cementitious material should be sufficient for efflorescence and absorption control. If water repellency is required dosage may be increased to 750 ml - 2000 ml /100 kg of cementitious material . Actual dosage rate will vary based upon mix design. Proper dosage should always be verified by trial batch to ensure desired performance is achieved.
5.4 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.5 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sika® Masonry AU 1, April 2023, Version 01.02, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/q/sika_masonry_au_1.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sika Masonry AU 1, version 05/08/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/5/MSDS%20Sika%C2%AE%20Masonry%20AU%201%20GHS7.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.1, and include the records in the project documentation.
